newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore HSFO up on crude gains, supplies healthy.
newsitem.headline: Singapore HSFO up on crude gains, supplies healthy.

text.p: High sulphur fuel oil prices were assessed higher on Friday as sentiment was strong on firm overnight crude levels and paper indications, traders said.
Physical 180-centistoke cargoes for October lifting were quoted at $118-$122 per tonne on Thursday. On Friday, offers were seen at $122 against bids at $121 on Friday.
Some traders said current prices were assessed too high. They said current fundamentals did not reflect the firm prices.
"There are more supplies than demand," said a trader. "Prices have risen purely on firm sentiment, triggered by the overall high prices on the energy futures." the trader said.
He cited the firm NYMEX heating oil, which reached a five-year high earlier this week, and firm IPE gas oil prices which had also helped fuel strong physical fuel oil prices in the European market.
Another traders said, trading firms in Singapore interested in seeing higher prices may take the opportunity to raise bids and offers.
But Kuwait and Venezuelan cargoes remained unsold, traders said, while demand from China remained thin.
October swaps were also quoted higher at $118-$118.50, compared with Thursday's $118.75/$119.50.
Low sulphur waxy residue (LSWR) prices were also firmer, driven by high crude prices. Traders said South Korea's KEPCO and Taiwan's tender to buy LSWR may help firm prices.
